theory.intro: The **interquartile range (IQR)** measures the spread of the middle $50\%$ of an ordered dataset. It has less impact from extreme values than the range.
facts: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$, the distance between the upper and lower quartiles.
The **range** ($\text{Max} - \text{Min}$) uses the two most extreme values, so a single outlier can inflate it.
The **IQR** is less affected by extreme values than the range. Adding a value can change the quartile positions.
State the IQR with units when the data carry units, for example $^{\circ}\text{C}$ or minutes.
steps: Find $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ (sort the data first if needed)

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the interquartile range in each case.
a. $Q_1 = 13.6$ minutes and $Q_3 = 28.9$ minutes.
b. Temperatures ($^{\circ}\text{C}$): $7, -4, 12, 1, -8, 4, 9, -1, 15$.
c. Times (minutes), in ascending order: $5.2, 7.4, 9.6, 12.3, 14.8, 17.5, 21.1, 24.6$.

Two groups record travel times (minutes).
Group A: $8, 11, 13, 16, 18, 20, 22, 43$.
Group B: $6, 10, 14, 19, 24, 28, 32, 37$.
Find each range and IQR. Which group's middle $50\%$ of times is more consistent? Explain why range and IQR give different comparisons.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Group A: $\text{Range} = 43 - 8 = 35$ minutes.
$Q_1 = \frac{11+13}{2} = 12$, $Q_3 = \frac{20+22}{2} = 21$.
$\text{IQR}_A = 21 - 12 = 9$ minutes.
Group B: $\text{Range} = 37 - 6 = 31$ minutes.
$Q_1 = \frac{10+14}{2} = 12$, $Q_3 = \frac{28+32}{2} = 30$.
$\text{IQR}_B = 30 - 12 = 18$ minutes.
Group A has the smaller IQR, so its middle $50\%$ of times is more consistent. Its range is larger because of the extreme time of $43$ minutes. Range uses the two extremes; IQR uses the middle half.

workedExamples.question_text:
The ordered scores are $4, 7, 11, 15, 18, 22, 27, 31$.
a. Find the range and IQR.
b. Add a score of $49$. Find the new range and IQR. Explain whether the IQR is unchanged.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a. $\text{Range} = 31 - 4 = 27$.
Lower half: $4, 7, 11, 15$; upper half: $18, 22, 27, 31$.
$Q_1 = \frac{7+11}{2} = 9$, $Q_3 = \frac{22+27}{2} = 24.5$.
$\text{IQR} = 24.5 - 9 = 15.5$.
b. New ordered scores: $4, 7, 11, 15, 18, 22, 27, 31, 49$.
$\text{Range} = 49 - 4 = 45$.
Leave out the single middle score, $18$.
Lower half: $4, 7, 11, 15$; upper half: $22, 27, 31, 49$.
$Q_1 = 9$, $Q_3 = \frac{27+31}{2} = 29$.
$\text{IQR} = 29 - 9 = 20$.
The range increases by $18$ and the IQR increases by $4.5$. Adding a score changes the quartile positions, so the IQR need not stay unchanged.

mastery.question_text:
The daily temperatures ($^{\circ}\text{C}$) for $9$ days, listed in ascending order, are:
$9, 12, 14, 16, 16, 17, 19, 21, 23$
A $10$th day, an unseasonal heatwave of $40^{\circ}\text{C}$, is added to the dataset.
Compare how the range and the interquartile range change, and explain why.
mastery.solution_text:
Before: $\text{Range} = 23 - 9 = 14^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_1 = 13^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_3 = 20^{\circ}\text{C}$, $\text{IQR} = 7^{\circ}\text{C}$
After adding $40^{\circ}\text{C}$: $\text{Range} = 40 - 9 = 31^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_1 = 14^{\circ}\text{C}$, $Q_3 = 21^{\circ}\text{C}$, $\text{IQR} = 7^{\circ}\text{C}$
The range more than doubles, from $14^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $31^{\circ}\text{C}$, because it depends directly on the new maximum
Both quartiles increase by $1^{\circ}\text{C}$, so their difference stays at $7^{\circ}\text{C}$. In this dataset, the range changes but the IQR does not.

mastery.question_text:
Two cities' daily temperatures ($^{\circ}\text{C}$) over $8$ days are recorded.
City A: $18, 19, 19, 20, 21, 21, 22, 23$
City B: $10, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 35$
Compare the interquartile ranges to determine which city has more consistent daily temperatures.
mastery.solution_text:
City A: $Q_1 = 19$, $Q_3 = 21.5$
$\text{IQR}_A = 21.5 - 19 = 2.5^{\circ}\text{C}$
City B: $Q_1 = 16.5$, $Q_3 = 28.5$
$\text{IQR}_B = 28.5 - 16.5 = 12^{\circ}\text{C}$
City A has the smaller IQR, so its middle $50\%$ of temperatures are far less spread out
City A has more consistent daily temperatures.
